notes: Asset-type registry. Adding a type is a data change here plus (when JSON Schema must enumerate it) one line in schemas/asset-plan.schema.json. core_pack.mjs, the core-pack provider, and media-use registry types all derive from this file — do not hard-code a second type list anywhere.

discovery_modes.keyword: Large sets. Agent narrows with --query; tags/aliases carry recall.
discovery_modes.table: Small sets. --type returns the whole table so the agent can reason across it.
discovery_modes.sheet: Visual choice. --query --sheet renders a contact sheet of the candidates; the agent reads the image and picks a cell.

icon.hf_usage: Inline the SVG for per-path animation, or reference it with /background-image when it is decoration.
icon.notes: Semantic lookup: the agent knows the concept ("trash") and needs the mark. Not brand logos — those stay in the media-use logo cascade.

shape.hf_usage: Inline for morph/draw animation; background-image when static. Tint with currentColor or a CSS custom property rather than editing the file.
shape.notes: Geometric lookup, not semantic: blobs, waves, dividers, grids, arrows, frames. Kept apart from icon because the query vocabulary is shape language, not concept language.

font.hf_usage: Declare @font-face with the frozen local path. Do not rely on the compiler's implicit Google fetch for anything that must render in a distributed/cloud render.
font.notes: Admit only families HyperFrames does NOT pre-bundle (see hyperframes-creative/references/typography.md). Re-shipping a pre-bundled family is pure install weight.

texture.hf_usage: background-image on an untimed wrapper. Tileable entries take background-repeat; full-frame entries take background-size: cover.
texture.notes: A surface the frame sits ON. Tileability is a property (geometry.tileable), not a separate type — query it with --tileable.
texture.acquisition_note: Not preinstalled by policy: a texture is film-specific (its palette, grain, and era must match one frame), so a shipped set is both large and usually wrong. Resolves through VidMuse image generation and freezes into the project. A project may still adopt its own file with `resolve --from`, and the Creator Library may hold licensed sets.

overlay.hf_usage: Absolutely-positioned layer above the content with mix-blend-mode (overlay/soft-light/screen) and a tuned opacity.
overlay.notes: A layer that sits ON TOP and changes how the frame reads: grain, noise, scanlines, dust, light leaks. Alpha is mandatory — an overlay without it is opaque and useless.
overlay.acquisition_note: Not preinstalled by policy. Prefer CSS/canvas for plain grain, noise, and scanlines — parametric, zero bytes, and tunable per frame (hyperframes-registry ships a grain-overlay component). Reach for generation only when the look cannot be produced procedurally.

lottie.hf_usage: Load with lottie-web or a dotLottie player, then register the instance on window.__hfLottie so HyperFrames can seek it.
lottie.usage_contract: autoplay: false, loop: false, and window.__hfLottie.push(anim) are all mandatory. Anything left on autoplay/loop runs in wall-clock time and renders non-deterministically. The adapter seeks absolute time — no modulo loop, no playback-rate scaling — so bake repeating cycles into the asset. See hyperframes-animation/adapters/lottie.md.
lottie.notes: Assets with their own pre-baked timeline (typically After Effects exports).

brand.hf_usage: Inline SVG or . A mono mark inherits currentColor; a color mark must not be recolored. Keep clear space around it.
brand.notes: Identity search, not browsing: the caller knows which company they mean. Query results apply a relevance floor so near-miss brands are dropped rather than offered — a wrong mark is a factual error in the film, unlike a near-miss icon which is only a stylistic one.
brand.acquisition_note: The live logo cascade (Lobe Icons → SVGL → Simple Icons → GitHub avatar → favicon) resolves first and stays authoritative, because brand marks change and new models appear constantly. The preinstalled set is a curated floor of settled brands — ONE mark each, color where upstream has it and mono for brands that are monochrome by design — reached only when offline or when every live tier misses. Wordmarks and lockups are not frozen: variant choice is what the live cascade is for. VidMuse-owned marks also live here.

sfx.hf_usage: A separate <audio> element that is a DIRECT child of the composition root, with data-start/data-duration/data-track-index.
sfx.notes: Indexed read-only from media-use, which already owns the files, the bundled-sfx provider, and the doctor check. Not copied here — copying would create a permanent re-vendor patch.

palette.hf_usage: Feed hex values into a color-typed data-composition-variables entry, a CSS custom property, or a Tailwind v4 @theme block.
palette.notes: Data, not files. Indexed read-only from hyperframes-creative, which owns the palettes and the frame-preset colors: blocks.

not_indexed.logo: Unbounded set requiring exact entity matching. Resolved live through the media-use cascade (Lobe Icons -> SVGL -> Simple Icons -> GitHub avatar -> favicon). A local copy would go stale and invite wrong-identity substitution.
not_indexed.image: Project-specific photography. No pre-install reuse value; goes through a provider or generation per film.
not_indexed.bgm: Generated per film by the VidMuse CLI.
not_indexed.voice: Generated per film by the VidMuse CLI.
not_indexed.video: Generated per film by the VidMuse CLI.
not_indexed.grade: Owned by media-use as parametric look specs (media-use/luts/index.json).
not_indexed.lut: Owned by media-use as parametric look specs (media-use/luts/index.json).
not_indexed.hdri: Single files run from several MB to tens of MB, which breaks the per-pack size budget. Three.js also wants these preloaded per project rather than resolved at seek time — project freeze is the right layer.
not_indexed.model3d: Same size argument as hdri; .gltf/.glb belong to a project, not to every plugin install.
not_indexed.map: No geojson/topojson/d3-geo consumer exists anywhere in the bundled HyperFrames skills. A static map render is a texture; live map data is project data. Do not create the category before a consumer exists.
